entries.text: We are to pray for deliverance from our enemies.

text.text: And they cried unto the Lord, and said, We have sinned, because we have forsaken the Lord, and have served Baalim and Ashtaroth: but now deliver us out of the hand of our enemies, and we will serve thee.
And the Lord sent Jerubbaal, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered you out of the hand of your enemies on every side, and ye dwelled safe.
I have called upon thee, for thou wilt hear me, O God: incline thine ear unto me, and hear my speech.
Shew thy marvellous lovingkindness, O thou that savest by thy right hand them which put their trust in thee from those that rise up against them.
Keep me as the apple of the eye, hide me under the shadow of thy wings,
From the wicked that oppress me, from my deadly enemies, who compass me about.
But in mine adversity they rejoiced, and gathered themselves together: yea, the abjects gathered themselves together against me, and I knew it not; they did tear me, and ceased not:
With hypocritical mockers in feasts, they gnashed upon me with their teeth.
Lord, how long wilt thou look on? rescue my soul from their destructions, my darling from the lions.
Deliver me from mine enemies, O my God: defend me from them that rise up against me.
Hear my voice, O God, in my prayer: preserve my life from fear of the enemy.
Then said Saul, I have sinned: return, my son David: for I will no more do thee harm, because my soul was precious in thine eyes this day: behold, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly.
Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head.
Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.

entries.text: Christ's enemies are to be destroyed.

text.text: But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.

caseRefs.name: Sihon and Og
caseRefs.charge: Refusing Israel passage and coming out to battle against them

caseRefs.name: The Midianites, in the matter of Peor
caseRefs.charge: Beguiling Israel with their wiles into fornication and the worship of Baal-peor

caseRefs.name: Eglon king of Moab
caseRefs.charge: Possessing the city of palm trees and taking tribute of Israel eighteen years

caseRefs.name: Jabin and Sisera
caseRefs.charge: Mightily oppressing Israel twenty years with nine hundred chariots of iron

caseRefs.name: Jael
caseRefs.charge: Blessed above women in the tent: the nail, the hammer, and Sisera

caseRefs.name: Agag king of the Amalekites
caseRefs.charge: The sword that made women childless

caseRefs.name: Goliath of Gath
caseRefs.charge: Defying the armies of the living God, morning and evening, forty days

caseRefs.name: Ben-hadad and the Syrians at Aphek
caseRefs.charge: Saying the Lord is a god of the hills and not of the valleys

caseRefs.name: Hazael king of Syria
caseRefs.charge: Smothering his master to take the throne, and doing to Israel the evil Elisha wept over

caseRefs.name: Hoshea, last king of Israel
caseRefs.charge: Doing evil in the sight of the Lord; conspiring with Egypt against Assyria

caseRefs.name: Sennacherib and Rabshakeh
caseRefs.charge: Reproaching the living God; setting him among the gods of the nations that could not save

caseRefs.name: Moab and Ammon
caseRefs.charge: Magnifying themselves against the Lord and against his people; rejoicing over the sanctuary when it was profaned

caseRefs.name: Mordecai and Esther
caseRefs.charge: Mordecai: bowing not to Haman. Esther: going in to the king against the law, after three days' fast: if I perish, I perish

caseRefs.name: Apollonius
caseRefs.charge: Falling upon Jerusalem on the Sabbath under a pretence of peace; slaying a great multitude; taking women and children captive

caseRefs.name: Timotheus
caseRefs.charge: Gathering the heathen to root out the Jews; a second campaign after being once spared
